hero.headline: US launches second round of strikes on Iran in three days
hero.body:
Israel launched a new wave of strikes targeting Iranian military infrastructure across Tehran shortly after Donald Trump announced a pause in American attacks on energy facilities. The Israeli military said it would continue operations according to government directives, even as the US administration signaled a shift in its negotiating approach.

Trump stated that Washington and Tehran had engaged in "very good and productive conversations" over the previous two days. He instructed the Department of Defense to postpone strikes against Iranian power plants and energy infrastructure for five days, pending the success of ongoing discussions. This announcement came approximately 40 minutes before the Israeli Defense Forces declared on social media that they had "just begun another wave of strikes targeting infrastructure of the Iranian terror regime across Tehran."

An Israeli military official told the Times of Israel that the IDF could not comment on the US president's announcement, describing it as a "political echelon matter." The official stated the military was "operating in accordance with the directives of Israel's political leadership and will continue to strike in Iran according to its plans until instructed otherwise." The IDF indicated that energy infrastructure would be spared from Israeli attacks, potentially aligning with Washington's new position.

According to Israeli military statements released Monday, the strikes targeted multiple military sites including an Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps air defence and ground forces headquarters, a Quds Force base and intelligence site, and a defence ministry missile production facility. An Al Jazeera Arabic correspondent in Tehran reported that explosions in the capital were of "unprecedented" size and volume.

The escalation came as Iran's Revolutionary Guards announced a new attack on Israeli targets. The military action underscores the fragile nature of ceasefire arrangements between the parties even as diplomatic efforts continue to resolve the three-month conflict.

The Israeli military claimed it had destroyed or rendered inoperable approximately 330 of Iran's estimated 470 ballistic missile launchers since the war began. More than half were destroyed through airstrikes, while others were disabled after entrances to underground storage sites were targeted. The military said it continues pursuing the remaining launchers as missile fire on Israel has decreased to roughly 10 per day from approximately 90 at the conflict's start.

Separately, Israel has maintained its military campaign against Hezbollah in Lebanon. Israeli strikes hit Beirut's southern suburbs on Monday, the first attack on the stronghold in several days. Lebanon's health ministry reported one death from the strikes.

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for Israeli sovereignty over southern Lebanese territory, saying the military campaign "needs to end with a different reality entirely" and proposing the Litani River as Israel's new border. The statement signals potential territorial ambitions beyond immediate military objectives.

cards.headline: Oil prices rise after US airstrikes on Iran during peace talks
cards.body:
Oil prices increased after the United States launched new military strikes against Iran, even as the two countries engage in peace negotiations. The attacks occurred despite an active ceasefire between Washington and Tehran.

The strikes represent a contradiction in US policy, with military action continuing while diplomatic talks proceed. The ceasefire had been in place as negotiators from both nations worked toward a broader agreement.

Oil markets reacted to the military escalation with price increases, reflecting investor concern about potential disruptions to global energy supplies. The Persian Gulf region accounts for a significant portion of worldwide oil production and transport.

Earlier market movements had shown oil futures falling on optimism about a potential US-Iran agreement. Asian stock markets declined following news of the strikes, while oil prices gained more than one dollar per barrel.

The timing of the military action during active peace talks adds uncertainty to the negotiating process. Both countries had been working to reduce tensions that have affected regional stability and global energy markets.

The strikes mark a continuation of hostilities in the Gulf region despite diplomatic efforts. Market analysts are monitoring the situation for signs of whether peace negotiations will continue or if the military action signals a breakdown in the diplomatic process.

Investors responded to the mixed signals from Washington with caution. The combination of peace talks and military strikes creates unpredictability for markets that had begun pricing in reduced tensions between the two nations.

The situation remains fluid as both military operations and diplomatic channels appear to be active simultaneously. Oil traders are watching for further developments that could affect supply routes and production in the region.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to multiple reports.

CNN first reported the investigation, which focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition as part of her two civil lawsuits against Trump. The probe marks a significant turn in the yearslong legal battle between Carroll and the president.

Carroll, a former magazine columnist, has accused Trump of sexually assaulting her in a New York department store dressing room in the mid-1990s. Trump has denied the allegations. Carroll sued Trump for defamation after he called her a liar and questioned her credibility. She later filed a second lawsuit against him under New York's Adult Survivors Act, which temporarily allowed victims of sexual assault to sue regardless of when the alleged abuse occurred.

The investigation centers on statements Carroll made under oath during depositions related to these civil cases. Perjury, the act of lying under oath, is a federal crime that can carry significant penalties including imprisonment.

The Justice Department's decision to investigate a prominent accuser of the president raises questions about the independence of federal law enforcement. Critics have long warned about potential conflicts of interest when the Justice Department investigates cases involving the president or his personal interests.

Carroll's legal team has not publicly commented on the investigation. The Justice Department declined to provide details about the scope or status of the probe.

The investigation comes as Trump has called for prosecutions of various political opponents and critics. During his campaign and presidency, Trump has repeatedly attacked Carroll and questioned her motives for bringing the lawsuits.

The civil cases between Trump and Carroll have proceeded through federal courts in New York. A jury previously found Trump liable for sexual abuse and defamation in one of the cases, awarding Carroll millions of dollars in damages. Trump has appealed that verdict.

Perjury investigations typically involve detailed review of sworn testimony, supporting documents, and other evidence to determine whether false statements were made knowingly and materially. Federal prosecutors must prove that any false statements were deliberate rather than mistaken or misremembered.

cards.headline: U.S. military shoots down Iranian drones, strikes launch site amid peace negotiations
cards.teaser: U.S. forces intercepted four Iranian attack drones and destroyed a ground control station as negotiations to end the conflict continue.
cards.body:
The U.S. military intercepted four Iranian attack drones targeting a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz and destroyed a ground control station in Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone. This marked the second military engagement between U.S. and Iranian forces in two days.

The clashes occur while the United States and Iran pursue negotiations to resolve their conflict. During a Cabinet meeting, President Trump signaled a tougher stance on Iran, contradicting his earlier weekend statements suggesting an agreement was imminent. U.S. Central Command confirmed its forces responded to the drone threat in the strategically vital shipping corridor.

cards.headline: Israel orders evacuations in southern Lebanon
cards.teaser: The Israeli military designated areas south of the Zahrani River as combat zones and warned Hezbollah of potential strikes.
cards.body:
Israel's military has declared areas south of the Zahrani River in southern Lebanon to be combat zones and issued evacuation orders for the affected regions. The designation makes clear that civilians in these territories should leave.

The Israeli military has warned Hezbollah of additional strikes in the area. The evacuation order reflects the escalating military operations between Israel and the militant group in Lebanon's south.

cards.headline: Former CIA officer arrested with $40 million in gold bars at home
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a former CIA official with stealing 300 gold bars worth approximately $40 million from the agency.
cards.body:
The FBI arrested David Rush, a former CIA officer, after discovering $40 million worth of gold bars in his home. Prosecutors allege Rush stole roughly 300 gold bars from the agency during his tenure.

According to the criminal complaint, Rush allegedly defrauded the government by lying about his credentials. The case represents one of the largest theft cases involving a former US intelligence official. Federal authorities have not disclosed how long the alleged theft occurred or how Rush managed to remove the gold from CIA facilities.

cards.headline: Washington paper mill implosion leaves 11 workers presumed dead
cards.teaser: A chemical tank rupture at a Longview paper mill could be the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history.
cards.body:
A tank ruptured at a paper mill in Longview, Washington, in what the governor called a potential "deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history." One worker was confirmed killed, while nine others remain missing. Nine additional workers were injured in the incident.

The disaster involved white liquor, a caustic chemical used in paper manufacturing. Rescue operations have transitioned to recovery efforts, and contaminated water from the rupture has been flushed through Longview's water system.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after $1.2 million profit on Polymarket
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he made $1.2 million through bets placed on Polymarket, a prediction market platform.

According to the complaint, the engineer wagered over $2.7 million on outcomes related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign. The charges suggest the employee used non-public information about the company's planned announcements to place informed bets on the platform.

Polymarket allows users to bet on real-world events, including corporate announcements, political outcomes, and cultural trends. The platform has grown in popularity as a venue for prediction markets, where participants can profit from correctly forecasting future events.

The case represents one of the first major insider trading prosecutions involving prediction markets rather than traditional stock trading. Prosecutors allege the Google employee exploited his position at the company to gain access to confidential information about which search terms and topics would be featured in the annual Year in Search report.

The Year in Search campaign is released by Google each year, highlighting the most popular search queries and trending topics over the previous 12 months. The report typically generates significant media attention and public interest.

By placing large wagers on Polymarket before the information became public, the engineer allegedly profited from advance knowledge of the campaign's contents. The complaint indicates he risked more than $2.7 million across multiple bets to generate the $1.2 million in profits.

Insider trading laws prohibit individuals from trading securities or other instruments based on material non-public information. While prediction markets operate differently from stock markets, prosecutors appear to be applying similar legal standards to wagers that rely on confidential corporate information.

The charges highlight growing regulatory scrutiny of prediction markets and how insider information might be exploited on these platforms. As prediction markets expand beyond traditional betting on elections and sports, prosecutors are examining whether existing securities laws apply to these new forms of wagering on corporate and economic events.

cards.headline: Packers running back Josh Jacobs arrested on domestic violence charges
cards.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was arrested and faces multiple domestic violence charges, including felony strangulation. He was released from custody on Wednesday as the district attorney continues to review the case.

Jacobs faces five charges in total related to the domestic violence incident. The felony strangulation charge represents the most serious allegation among them. The Packers running back was taken into police custody earlier this week.

Authorities released Jacobs from jail on Wednesday while the investigation proceeds. The district attorney has not yet filed formal charges and is still evaluating the evidence in the case.

Jacobs joined the Packers before the 2025 season after spending his first five NFL seasons with the Las Vegas Raiders. He rushed for over 1,500 yards in 2022 and earned Pro Bowl honors that year.

The Packers have not publicly commented on Jacobs' arrest or his status with the team. The NFL has also not announced whether it will conduct its own investigation under the league's personal conduct policy.

Domestic violence cases in professional sports typically trigger both criminal proceedings and league discipline. The NFL's personal conduct policy allows the commissioner to place players on paid leave during investigations and to suspend players even if criminal charges are not filed.

The timing of the arrest comes during the offseason, with organized team activities underway across the league. Teams are preparing for training camps that will begin in July ahead of the 2026 season.

Jacobs' legal situation remains unresolved as prosecutors determine whether to move forward with charges. The district attorney's office has not provided a timeline for when a charging decision will be made.

cards.headline: Crystal Palace win Conference League with victory over Rayo Vallecano
cards.teaser: Jean-Philippe Mateta scored as Crystal Palace won the European club competition under manager Oliver Glasner.
cards.body:
Crystal Palace won their first European trophy by defeating Rayo Vallecano 1-0 in the Conference League final in Leipzig. Jean-Philippe Mateta scored the decisive goal in what proved to be manager Oliver Glasner's final match in charge.

The victory was particularly significant for Palace, who finished 15th in the Premier League. As Conference League winners, they have secured a place in next season's Europa League—a spot they would not have earned through their league position. The triumph comes a year after Palace were denied Europa League qualification despite winning the FA Cup due to UEFA's multi-club ownership regulations.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to reopen Trump IRS lawsuit over settlement creating $1.776 billion fund
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges petitioned a court to investigate a settlement between President Trump and the IRS.
cards.body:
Revised Card Text

A bipartisan group of former federal judges has petitioned a court to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. They argue the administration bypassed judicial oversight by settling the case and establishing a $1.776 billion fund without proper court involvement.

The fund, announced by the Department of Justice in May, is described as compensation for alleged "victims of lawfare and weaponization." The petition raises concerns about whether the settlement followed appropriate legal procedures for resolving disputes between the executive branch and federal agencies.

cards.headline: Australia files $2 billion lawsuit against 3M over chemical contamination
cards.teaser: The government sued the US manufacturer over alleged contamination from firefighting foam at defense sites.
cards.body:
The Australian government has launched legal action against 3M, seeking more than A$2 billion in damages over contamination at defence bases. The case centers on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly known as "forever chemicals," which were used in firefighting foam at military facilities.

This represents the largest legal claim ever brought by the Australian government. Attorney General Michelle Rowland announced the lawsuit against the multinational manufacturer, marking a significant action against the chemical contamination at defence sites.

cards.headline: Pakistan and Afghanistan continue fighting despite Chinese mediation
cards.teaser: Neither country has backed down months after Pakistan declared open war on Afghanistan.
cards.body:
Pakistan and Afghanistan remain in conflict months after Pakistan declared open war. Neither side shows willingness to stand down despite ongoing tensions.

China has attempted to mediate between the two countries without success. The fighting continues as diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict have failed to produce a ceasefire or resolution.

cards.headline: Ken Paxton wins Texas Senate primary, reshaping Republican landscape
cards.teaser: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton defeated Senator John Cornyn in a runoff, demonstrating Trump's continued influence over the Republican Party.
cards.body:
Ken Paxton won the Republican primary runoff for US Senate in Texas, defeating incumbent John Cornyn. The outcome underscores President Trump's grip on the Republican Party and marks a significant shift in Texas politics. Republicans have begun reconciling with Paxton after what multiple outlets described as a brutal primary campaign.

Democrats changed their messaging strategy following Paxton's victory. Representative James Talarico, running on the Democratic side, adjusted his campaign approach after the primary results. Analysts are now examining Democratic chances of defeating Paxton in the general election, though Texas remains a Republican-leaning state.

cards.headline: China's pork prices hit 16-year low
cards.teaser: Pork prices in China reached their lowest level in 16 years, reflecting weak consumer spending and oversupply.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

Pork prices in China fell to a 16-year low, driven by weak consumer spending and an oversupply of hogs. The decline represents a significant shift in a key inflation indicator for the country's economy.

The price drop stems from two factors: reduced consumer demand and excess production capacity in the hog industry. Pork serves as an important measure of inflation in China, where it is a dietary staple and closely watched economic indicator.

---

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: The state civil rights agency defeated Tesla's attempt to throw out the case, with trial expected in July.
cards.body:
A California court rejected Tesla's attempt to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit brought by the state's civil rights agency. The agency hailed the decision as a win over the electric vehicle manufacturer.

The case is now expected to proceed to trial in July. California's civil rights agency filed the lawsuit alleging discriminatory practices at Tesla facilities within the state.

cards.headline: Bipartisan Senate bill proposes reforms for college sports including salary cap and transfer limits
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell introduced legislation to address compensation, transfers and enforcement in college athletics.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell released a bipartisan bill targeting college sports reform. The legislation proposes creating a salary cap system and limiting player transfers between schools.

The bill also includes provisions aimed at preventing coach poaching after recent high-profile moves, including Lane Kiffin's jump to LSU. The legislation addresses eligibility rules and enforcement mechanisms across college athletics programs.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey subpoena FIFA over World Cup ticket pricing
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from both states opened an investigation into complaints about high ticket prices for the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
New York and New Jersey's attorneys general have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The subpoena seeks information about FIFA's ticket sales and pricing strategies, with the probe announced by New York's Letitia James and New Jersey's Jennifer Davenport.

The investigation focuses on matches at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Complaints center on fans being misled about seat locations and FIFA's public messaging contributing to inflated ticket prices throughout the tournament.

cards.headline: Georgia coach Kirby Smart suggests SEC could leave NCAA
cards.teaser: The Georgia football coach said he would support the conference breaking away to operate under its own rules.
cards.body:
Georgia head football coach Kirby Smart raised the possibility of the SEC leaving the NCAA to operate independently. Smart said he would support the conference creating its own governance structure and playing by its own rules.

The comments come amid ongoing debates about conference expansion and how college athletics should be structured. Multiple sources reported that SEC leaders are discussing contingency plans, though no formal action has been taken toward separating from the NCAA.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A three-judge panel granted Mahmoud Khalil's request to stay out of custody while he petitions the Supreme Court.
cards.body:
Original Card Text Returned

A federal appeals court panel allowed pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free as he takes his case against the Trump administration to the Supreme Court. The three-judge panel from the 3rd Circuit included appointees of President Trump, former President George W. Bush, and former President Joe Biden.

Judges Stephanos Bibas, Arianna Freeman, and Thomas Hardiman granted the stay, permitting Khalil to avoid custody while pursuing his appeal to the nation's highest court. The decision represents a temporary victory for Khalil in his ongoing legal battle with federal authorities.

---

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared Joe Biden was having stroke during debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by her husband's performance against Donald Trump in 2024.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden said she was "frightened" while watching Joe Biden's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. She told CBS News that she had never seen her husband perform that way before or since, and thought he might have suffered a stroke during the televised event.

Biden made these comments in an interview set to air on Sunday.

cards.headline: Australia charges woman who returned from Syria with joining Islamic State
cards.teaser: The woman is among several groups who spent years in a Syrian camp before recent repatriation.
cards.body:
Australian authorities have charged a woman with joining the Islamic State following her return from Syria. The woman had spent years detained in a Syrian camp before being repatriated to Australia.

In recent months, multiple groups of women and children have been brought back to Australia from Syrian detention facilities. The charged woman is among those who were repatriated from these camps.

cards.headline: Iran restores internet access after 88-day shutdown
cards.teaser: The government ended a near-total internet blackout, though access remains limited and uncertain.
cards.body:
The Iranian government restored internet access after an 88-day shutdown that blocked news, television, and messaging services. Citizens can now connect with the outside world after the near-total blackout.

Access remains limited, with not all Iranians able to connect. Those who have regained internet service are uncertain how long the government will maintain the restored access.

cards.headline: China expands factory operations to overseas locations
cards.teaser: Chinese manufacturers are establishing production facilities abroad, raising concerns among international competitors.
cards.body:
Chinese companies are exporting their manufacturing operations by building factories across the world, prompting unease among competitors in those markets. The expansion represents a shift in how China participates in global trade.

China's trade surplus has grown to $1.2 trillion, triggering discussions about how the country manages its international commercial relationships. The factory exports come as China maintains a record trade surplus that continues to shape its global economic position.

cards.headline: Rivian to deliver first R2 SUVs on June 9
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker set a date for customer deliveries of its new model.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the date for first customer deliveries of its new R2 SUV. The company is expanding its vehicle lineup with this new model.

CEO RJ Scaringe has called the R2 "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date," underscoring the significance of this release for the electric vehicle maker.

cards.headline: Google's AI struggles with basic spelling and word recognition
cards.teaser: The company's AI search feature has faced difficulties with simple words like disregard, stop, and ignore.
cards.body:
Google's AI tools have encountered significant problems with fundamental language tasks, including an inability to correctly spell the word "Google" itself. The search feature has also struggled to process and define common words such as "disregard," "stop," and "ignore."

The issues have drawn widespread attention and criticism, with multiple reports documenting the degraded performance across Google's AI search capabilities. The problems raise questions about the reliability of Google's AI systems during a competitive period in the AI industry.

cards.headline: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson calls coaching changes a breath of fresh air
cards.teaser: The two-time MVP discussed offseason changes within the Baltimore organization and his commitment to the team.
cards.body:
Lamar Jackson described the coaching changes made by the Baltimore Ravens during the offseason as refreshing. The quarterback addressed the shifts in the organization's staff during organized team activities.

Jackson declined to discuss his contract negotiations but said his commitment to the Ravens has not changed. He indicated he wants to move past previous discussions about a fully guaranteed contract deal.

cards.headline: SEC leaders criticize College Football Playoff metrics explanation
cards.teaser: Conference officials objected to how the playoff selection committee explained its strength of schedule calculations.
cards.body:
Leaders from the Southeastern Conference criticized the College Football Playoff's explanation of how it weighs strength of schedule in team selection. The dispute centers on which metrics the committee uses to evaluate teams.

The debate has intensified as conferences discuss playoff expansion and selection criteria. SEC officials argue the current system does not adequately account for the difficulty of their conference schedule compared to teams in other leagues.

cards.headline: Tennis player Jakub Mensik collapses on court after French Open win
cards.teaser: The player said his body shut down following a second-round match played in high heat at the Paris tournament.
cards.body:
Jakub Mensik collapsed on court after winning his second-round match at the French Open in a gruelling five-set contest against Mariano Navone that lasted over four and a half hours. The tennis player said his body "just turned off" due to the extreme heat in Paris, and he required a wheelchair to return to the locker room.

Mensik criticised the conditions as "insane," highlighting the limited time available to cool down between changeovers. His collapse prompted calls from other players, including Novak Djokovic, for organisers to schedule more matches later in the day during periods of extreme heat.

cards.headline: Spielberg opposes AI as final creative authority in filmmaking
cards.body:
Director Steven Spielberg spoke against the use of artificial intelligence as a primary creative decision-maker in filmmaking during an appearance on the IMO podcast with Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson. The filmmaker drew a clear boundary on AI's role in Hollywood production.

Spielberg said he sees value in AI for solving medical problems but opposes its use in controlling creative processes. He stated he does not want AI taking over the creative process in Hollywood, though he did not specify which aspects of filmmaking he considers acceptable for AI assistance.

The director did not elaborate on what specific AI applications in film production concern him or whether he has encountered AI-driven decisions in his own work. He also did not address how the industry should regulate or limit AI use in creative roles.

Spielberg's comments come as studios and production companies increasingly experiment with AI tools for scriptwriting, visual effects, and post-production work. The technology has become a point of tension in Hollywood, particularly during recent labor negotiations between unions and studios.

The legendary filmmaker, whose career spans five decades and includes films like Jaws, E.T., and Schindler's List, has historically been known for hands-on creative control of his projects. His stance adds a prominent voice to the ongoing debate about technology's role in artistic industries.

Neither Spielberg nor the podcast hosts provided examples of how AI is currently being used in major film productions or what prompted his remarks. The director did not announce any specific actions he plans to take regarding AI use in his future projects.

cards.headline: Senator Andy Kim defends attendance at immigration detention facility protest after Homeland Security criticism
cards.teaser: The New Jersey senator responded to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin's remarks about his presence at a protest.
cards.body:
Senator Andy Kim of New Jersey defended his attendance at a protest outside a migrant detention facility after criticism from Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. During a White House Cabinet meeting, Mullin referenced Kim being hit by pepper ball spray at the demonstration.

Kim responded by emphasizing that his protest attendance was focused on the broader issue of immigration enforcement and detention conditions, not on his personal experience. The exchange underscored ongoing tensions between Democratic lawmakers and the Trump administration over how migrants are treated in federal custody.

cards.headline: California poll shows Becerra taking lead in governor's race
cards.teaser: A new poll indicates Xavier Becerra is opening a lead in California's gubernatorial race as the election approaches.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra has opened a lead in the California governor's race, according to a new poll. The race has shifted rapidly in recent weeks, with both candidates making campaign stops in the Bay Area as the election nears.

Democrats expressed confidence about the race despite the competition. CalMatters published a guide for undecided voters as interest in the election increases. Multiple news outlets have produced explainers to help voters understand the shifting dynamics of the gubernatorial contest.

cards.headline: Fair housing groups sue over federal lending rule changes
cards.teaser: Housing advocacy organizations filed a lawsuit challenging new federal rules they say weaken fair lending protections.
cards.body:
Fair housing groups brought legal action against federal regulators over a rule change they argue removes protections against lending discrimination. The lawsuit targets the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau over modifications to small business lending data requirements.

The new rule narrows the scope of data collection requirements for small business lending. Housing advocates contend the changes weaken anti-discrimination regulations that had been in place to ensure equal access to credit.

cards.headline: Space stocks surge as SpaceX prepares for public offering
cards.teaser: Shares of space industry companies experienced sharp price increases ahead of SpaceX's anticipated IPO.
cards.body:
Stock prices for space industry companies including Rocket Lab and AST experienced significant gains, with some short sellers facing losses. The movements come as SpaceX prepares for what could be a record-breaking initial public offering.

Analysts have compared the trading activity to patterns seen in electric vehicle stocks during that sector's boom period. Market observers are watching multiple factors ahead of the SpaceX IPO, though some analysts have expressed reservations about valuations in the space sector.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: The Psyche probe sent back high-resolution views of the red planet on its way to an asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft captured detailed images of Mars during a flyby of the planet. The probe photographed views of Mars' south pole and other surface features as it passed the red planet.

The spacecraft is traveling to a distant asteroid and used Mars for a gravity assist maneuver. The flyby provided an opportunity to collect unique imagery of the planet from the probe's trajectory and instruments.

---

Note: The additional source material provided covers different NASA stories (wildfire damage imagery and lunar missions), not the Mars flyby. I've returned your original card text unchanged.

cards.headline: Triomics raises $22 million for cancer center AI tools
cards.teaser: The oncology AI company secured Series B funding led by Battery Ventures.
cards.body:
Triomics has secured $22 million in Series B funding to develop artificial intelligence tools for oncology settings. Battery Ventures led the investment round.

The company is building AI applications tailored specifically for cancer centers, with the funding supporting the development and deployment of these specialized tools at cancer treatment facilities.

cards.headline: ABC News wins eight awards at News Emmys, fourth straight for World News Tonight
cards.teaser: ABC News led the 47th annual News Emmy Awards with eight wins, while National Geographic earned seven awards.
cards.body:
ABC News claimed eight awards at the 47th annual News Emmy Awards. ABC World News Tonight With David Muir earned the outstanding live news program award for the fourth consecutive year.

National Geographic secured seven News Emmy awards, with Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller among its honored programs. The ceremony celebrated news programming across broadcast and cable networks.

cards.headline: Student journalist criticizes CBS News direction while accepting Mike Wallace scholarship
cards.teaser: A high school senior from Washington criticized CBS News during his acceptance speech for a journalism scholarship named after Mike Wallace.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, used his acceptance speech for the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards to criticize CBS News. Campos said the recent direction of the outlet stains the legacy of Mike Wallace, the legendary CBS journalist for whom the scholarship is named.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship. The award ceremony took place Wednesday night, and Campos reportedly impressed the audience with his remarks.

cards.headline: Nintendo adding Donkey Kong 64 to Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: The N64 game will join the subscription service's classic library on June 3.
cards.body:
Nintendo will add Donkey Kong 64 to its Switch Online subscription service next week. The Nintendo 64 game will become available to subscribers on June 3.

Donkey Kong 64 originally released in the 1990s for the N64 console. The game joins Nintendo's expanding library of classic titles available through the Switch Online Expansion Pack tier.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo responds to criticism over recent outfits
cards.teaser: Singer Olivia Rodrigo addressed backlash over her recent clothing choices, saying women should not be held responsible for how men perceive them.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo responded to criticism of her recent outfits, which drew accusations online that her clothing both infantilized and sexualized the singer. Rodrigo said women should not be responsible for some guy sexualizing them.

The star faced backlash from internet commenters who took issue with her clothing choices. Rodrigo did not specify which outfits prompted the criticism or provide details about where or when she made her comments.

cards.headline: Morris Day denies participation in National Mall concert despite being listed in lineup
cards.teaser: Singer Morris Day said he and the Time will not perform at a June concert on the National Mall, despite being announced as headliners.
cards.body:
Morris Day denied what he called rumors that he and the Time are set to play a Freedom 250 concert on the National Mall in June, even though organizers announced him as a headliner. Day said it is a no for him regarding the performance.

The concert is scheduled for June 27 as part of a 16-day patriotic fair in Washington celebrating the nation's 250th anniversary. The event has drawn controversy, though the source material does not specify the nature of the disputes.

cards.headline: Horror film Obsession sees rare box office increase in second weekend
cards.teaser: The film Obsession posted a second-weekend box office increase, a rare occurrence that has drawn comparisons to Sound of Freedom.
cards.body:
Obsession made history at the box office with a second-weekend spike, according to industry reports. The horror film became this summer's breakout box office hit, achieving something that has not been done since Sound of Freedom.

The film is now considered a record-breaking horror release. Box office analysts described the performance as a stunner, though specific revenue figures were not provided in the available information.

cards.headline: Performers announced for national 250th anniversary celebration on National Mall
cards.teaser: Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice are among performers scheduled for a concert celebrating the nation's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
A concert is planned for the National Mall as part of celebrations for the nation's 250th birthday. Performers scheduled to appear include Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice, along with other acts from the 1990s including C+C Music Factory and Milli Vanilli.

The event is part of a 16-day celebration called the Great American State Fair. Morris Day and the Time were listed in the lineup, but Morris Day has denied rumors of his participation.

cards.headline: Lebanese expect prolonged conflict despite US-Iran negotiations
cards.teaser: Residents doubt diplomatic efforts to end the wider war will bring peace as Israel-Hezbollah clashes intensify.
cards.body:

hero.headline: US launches second round of strikes on Iran in three days
hero.body:
The United States conducted military strikes targeting Iranian attack drones and a ground control station, marking the second offensive operation against Iranian territory in as many days, a US official confirmed.

The strikes targeted military infrastructure in southern Iran. US officials characterized the attacks as defensive measures taken in self-defense, though the timing raised questions about their impact on ongoing diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran.

The military action occurred despite a ceasefire agreement currently in place between the two nations. The US and Iran have been engaged in peace negotiations aimed at resolving a three-month conflict that has strained relations across the region.

The renewed hostilities complicate an already fragile diplomatic situation. While both countries have maintained the ceasefire framework, the continued military operations suggest security concerns persist on both sides. US officials maintained that the strikes were necessary defensive responses to perceived threats.

Energy markets reacted swiftly to news of the attacks. Oil prices rose following the announcement, reflecting broader concerns about potential disruption to regional energy supplies. The market volatility underscores investor anxiety about the stability of the ceasefire arrangement.

The strikes focused on Iranian drone capabilities, including active unmanned aircraft and the ground facilities used to operate them. This targeting strategy suggests the US military concentrated on disabling Iran's remote warfare capacity rather than broader infrastructure systems.

Both nations face mounting pressure to preserve the ceasefire while addressing legitimate security concerns. The diplomatic track remains open despite the military activity, with negotiators from both countries continuing discussions about establishing a more permanent peace settlement.

Iran had not issued a public response to the latest attacks at the time of reporting. The absence of immediate Iranian retaliation suggests both sides may be attempting to maintain enough stability for negotiations to continue.

The escalation comes as international attention focuses on the wider conflict and its regional implications. The continuation of military strikes during active peace talks creates uncertainty about the negotiating process and raises questions about each side's commitment to a diplomatic resolution.

Military analysts note that such defensive strikes often serve dual purposes in conflict situations: addressing immediate tactical threats while also signaling resolve to the opposing party. Whether these operations will ultimately strengthen or undermine the diplomatic process remains unclear.

The ceasefire between the US and Iran, despite its fragile nature, has held through multiple military incidents. The ability of both countries to maintain this framework while pursuing their respective security interests will likely determine whether the current negotiation phase can produce a lasting agreement.

The situation reflects the broader challenge facing both nations: balancing military requirements against diplomatic opportunities for conflict resolution.

cards.headline: Israel orders evacuations in southern Lebanon
cards.teaser: The Israeli military designated areas south of the Zahrani River as combat zones and warned Hezbollah of potential strikes.
cards.body:
Israel's military has declared areas south of the Zahrani River in southern Lebanon to be combat zones and issued evacuation orders for the affected regions. The designation makes clear that civilians in these territories should leave.

The Israeli military has warned Hezbollah of additional strikes in the area. The evacuation order reflects the escalating military operations between Israel and the militant group in Lebanon's south.

cards.headline: Australia files $2 billion lawsuit against 3M over chemical contamination
cards.teaser: The government sued the US manufacturer over alleged contamination from firefighting foam at defense sites.
cards.body:
The Australian government has launched legal action against 3M, seeking more than A$2 billion in damages over contamination at defence bases. The case centers on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly known as "forever chemicals," which were used in firefighting foam at military facilities.

This represents the largest legal claim ever brought by the Australian government. Attorney General Michelle Rowland announced the lawsuit against the multinational manufacturer, marking a significant action against the chemical contamination at defence sites.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared Joe Biden was having stroke during debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by her husband's performance against Donald Trump in 2024.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden said she was "frightened" while watching Joe Biden's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. She told CBS News that she had never seen her husband perform that way before or since, and thought he might have suffered a stroke during the televised event.

Biden made these comments in an interview set to air on Sunday.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with insider trading using internal data
cards.teaser: A longtime Google worker allegedly used company information to make $1.2 million on bets.
cards.body:
A Google engineer named Michele Spagnuolo was charged with fraud by federal prosecutors in New York. He allegedly used confidential company information to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform, and made approximately $1.2 million from wagers related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign.

According to the complaint, Spagnuolo risked over $2.7 million on these trades. Prosecutors allege he knew the outcomes of these bets before the general public because he had access to Google's confidential data about search-related trends.

cards.headline: Australia charges woman who returned from Syria with joining Islamic State
cards.teaser: The woman is among several groups who spent years in a Syrian camp before recent repatriation.
cards.body:
Australian authorities have charged a woman with joining the Islamic State following her return from Syria. The woman had spent years detained in a Syrian camp before being repatriated to Australia.

In recent months, multiple groups of women and children have been brought back to Australia from Syrian detention facilities. The charged woman is among those who were repatriated from these camps.

cards.headline: Pakistan and Afghanistan continue fighting despite Chinese mediation
cards.teaser: Neither country has backed down months after Pakistan declared open war on Afghanistan.
cards.body:
Pakistan and Afghanistan remain in conflict months after Pakistan declared open war. Neither side shows willingness to stand down despite ongoing tensions.

China has attempted to mediate between the two countries without success. The fighting continues as diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict have failed to produce a ceasefire or resolution.

cards.headline: Iran restores internet access after 88-day shutdown
cards.teaser: The government ended a near-total internet blackout, though access remains limited and uncertain.
cards.body:
The Iranian government restored internet access after an 88-day shutdown that blocked news, television, and messaging services. Citizens can now connect with the outside world after the near-total blackout.

Access remains limited, with not all Iranians able to connect. Those who have regained internet service are uncertain how long the government will maintain the restored access.

Lebanese citizens remain skeptical that US-Iran peace talks will resolve the conflict affecting their country. The fighting between Israeli forces and Hezbollah in southern Lebanon continues to intensify.

hero.headline: US launches second round of strikes on Iran in three days
hero.body:
Israel launched a new wave of strikes targeting Iranian military infrastructure across Tehran shortly after Donald Trump announced a pause in American attacks on energy facilities. The Israeli military said it would continue operations according to government directives, even as the US administration signaled a shift in its negotiating approach.

Trump stated that Washington and Tehran had engaged in "very good and productive conversations" over the previous two days. He instructed the Department of Defense to postpone strikes against Iranian power plants and energy infrastructure for five days, pending the success of ongoing discussions. This announcement came approximately 40 minutes before the Israeli Defense Forces declared on social media that they had "just begun another wave of strikes targeting infrastructure of the Iranian terror regime across Tehran."

An Israeli military official told the Times of Israel that the IDF could not comment on the US president's announcement, describing it as a "political echelon matter." The official stated the military was "operating in accordance with the directives of Israel's political leadership and will continue to strike in Iran according to its plans until instructed otherwise." The IDF indicated that energy infrastructure would be spared from Israeli attacks, potentially aligning with Washington's new position.

According to Israeli military statements released Monday, the strikes targeted multiple military sites including an Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps air defence and ground forces headquarters, a Quds Force base and intelligence site, and a defence ministry missile production facility. An Al Jazeera Arabic correspondent in Tehran reported that explosions in the capital were of "unprecedented" size and volume.

The escalation came as Iran's Revolutionary Guards announced a new attack on Israeli targets. The military action underscores the fragile nature of ceasefire arrangements between the parties even as diplomatic efforts continue to resolve the three-month conflict.

The Israeli military claimed it had destroyed or rendered inoperable approximately 330 of Iran's estimated 470 ballistic missile launchers since the war began. More than half were destroyed through airstrikes, while others were disabled after entrances to underground storage sites were targeted. The military said it continues pursuing the remaining launchers as missile fire on Israel has decreased to roughly 10 per day from approximately 90 at the conflict's start.

Separately, Israel has maintained its military campaign against Hezbollah in Lebanon. Israeli strikes hit Beirut's southern suburbs on Monday, the first attack on the stronghold in several days. Lebanon's health ministry reported one death from the strikes.

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for Israeli sovereignty over southern Lebanese territory, saying the military campaign "needs to end with a different reality entirely" and proposing the Litani River as Israel's new border. The statement signals potential territorial ambitions beyond immediate military objectives.

cards.headline: Former CIA officer arrested with $40 million in gold bars at home
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a former CIA official with stealing 300 gold bars worth approximately $40 million from the agency.
cards.body:
The FBI arrested David Rush, a former CIA officer, after discovering $40 million worth of gold bars in his home. Prosecutors allege Rush stole roughly 300 gold bars from the agency during his tenure.

According to the criminal complaint, Rush allegedly defrauded the government by lying about his credentials. The case represents one of the largest theft cases involving a former US intelligence official. Federal authorities have not disclosed how long the alleged theft occurred or how Rush managed to remove the gold from CIA facilities.

cards.headline: Jill Biden describes fearing stroke during 2024 debate performance
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened watching her husband's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News she was frightened while watching her husband's performance during the June 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she thought Joe Biden might have suffered a stroke, describing his faltering performance as unlike anything she had witnessed before or since.

Biden's debate performance raised concerns within the Democratic Party about his fitness to continue his reelection campaign, becoming a turning point in the presidential race.

cards.headline: Washington paper mill implosion leaves 11 workers presumed dead
cards.teaser: A chemical tank rupture at a Longview paper mill could be the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history.
cards.body:
A tank ruptured at a paper mill in Longview, Washington, in what the governor called a potential "deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history." One worker was confirmed killed, while nine others remain missing. Nine additional workers were injured in the incident.

The disaster involved white liquor, a caustic chemical used in paper manufacturing. Rescue operations have transitioned to recovery efforts, and contaminated water from the rupture has been flushed through Longview's water system.

cards.headline: Ken Paxton wins Texas Senate primary, reshaping Republican landscape
cards.teaser: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton defeated Senator John Cornyn in a runoff, demonstrating Trump's continued influence over the Republican Party.
cards.body:
Ken Paxton won the Republican primary runoff for US Senate in Texas, defeating incumbent John Cornyn. The outcome underscores President Trump's grip on the Republican Party and marks a significant shift in Texas politics. Republicans have begun reconciling with Paxton after what multiple outlets described as a brutal primary campaign.

Democrats changed their messaging strategy following Paxton's victory. Representative James Talarico, running on the Democratic side, adjusted his campaign approach after the primary results. Analysts are now examining Democratic chances of defeating Paxton in the general election, though Texas remains a Republican-leaning state.

cards.headline: California poll shows Becerra taking lead in governor's race
cards.teaser: A new poll indicates Xavier Becerra is opening a lead in California's gubernatorial race as the election approaches.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra has opened a lead in the California governor's race, according to a new poll. The race has shifted rapidly in recent weeks, with both candidates making campaign stops in the Bay Area as the election nears.

Democrats expressed confidence about the race despite the competition. CalMatters published a guide for undecided voters as interest in the election increases. Multiple news outlets have produced explainers to help voters understand the shifting dynamics of the gubernatorial contest.

cards.headline: Google employee charged over insider trades on Polymarket
cards.teaser: The Justice Department charged a Google staffer with using insider information to net $1.2 million through prediction market trades.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he allegedly used confidential information about the company's 2025 Year in Search campaign to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The engineer risked over $2.7 million in wagers and made approximately $1.2 million in profits.

This marks the second known criminal case in which the Justice Department has pursued insider trading charges related to prediction market activity. The case underscores the government's approach to applying securities enforcement rules to prediction markets as they gain prominence.

hero.headline: Oil prices rise after US airstrikes on Iran during peace talks
hero.body:
Oil prices increased after the United States launched new military strikes against Iran, even as the two countries engage in peace negotiations. The attacks occurred despite an active ceasefire between Washington and Tehran.

The strikes represent a contradiction in US policy, with military action continuing while diplomatic talks proceed. The ceasefire had been in place as negotiators from both nations worked toward a broader agreement.

Oil markets reacted to the military escalation with price increases, reflecting investor concern about potential disruptions to global energy supplies. The Persian Gulf region accounts for a significant portion of worldwide oil production and transport.

Earlier market movements had shown oil futures falling on optimism about a potential US-Iran agreement. Asian stock markets declined following news of the strikes, while oil prices gained more than one dollar per barrel.

The timing of the military action during active peace talks adds uncertainty to the negotiating process. Both countries had been working to reduce tensions that have affected regional stability and global energy markets.

The strikes mark a continuation of hostilities in the Gulf region despite diplomatic efforts. Market analysts are monitoring the situation for signs of whether peace negotiations will continue or if the military action signals a breakdown in the diplomatic process.

Investors responded to the mixed signals from Washington with caution. The combination of peace talks and military strikes creates unpredictability for markets that had begun pricing in reduced tensions between the two nations.

The situation remains fluid as both military operations and diplomatic channels appear to be active simultaneously. Oil traders are watching for further developments that could affect supply routes and production in the region.

cards.teaser: The Australian government filed a $2 billion lawsuit against 3M over contamination from firefighting foam at defense installations.
cards.body:
Australia's government has launched legal action against US manufacturer 3M, seeking more than A$2 billion in damages over contamination at defence bases. Attorney General Michelle Rowland confirmed the case centres on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly known as "forever chemicals", which were used in firefighting foam at military facilities.

The lawsuit represents the largest legal claim ever brought by the Australian government. These chemicals persist in the environment and have caused contamination at defence installations across the country.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with insider trading on betting platform
cards.teaser: A longtime Google worker faces criminal charges for allegedly using internal company data to make $1.2 million on bets.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged Michele Spagnuolo, a Google information security engineer, with fraud after he allegedly used confidential company information to place bets on Polymarket. Spagnuolo wagered over $2.7 million on predictions related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign, winning approximately $1.2 million.

According to prosecutors, Spagnuolo accessed Google's internal data about search trends before the information became public, giving him an advantage in placing his bets. The case represents a novel application of insider trading laws to gambling on prediction markets rather than traditional securities.

cards.headline: China expands factory operations to overseas locations
cards.teaser: Chinese manufacturers are establishing production facilities abroad, raising concerns among international competitors.
cards.body:
Chinese companies are exporting their manufacturing operations by building factories across the world, prompting unease among competitors in those markets. The expansion represents a shift in how China participates in global trade.

China's trade surplus has grown to $1.2 trillion, triggering discussions about how the country manages its international commercial relationships. The factory exports come as China maintains a record trade surplus that continues to shape its global economic position.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey investigate FIFA over World Cup ticket sales
cards.teaser: State authorities are examining FIFA's ticket pricing and sales practices after reports fans were misled about seating.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The probe focuses on matches scheduled for MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, and was announced by New York's Letitia James and New Jersey's Jennifer Davenport.

Fans have reported being misled about seat locations and claim FIFA's messaging contributed to inflated ticket prices. Authorities issued a subpoena seeking information on FIFA's ticketing practices and sales procedures related to the tournament.

cards.headline: Fair housing groups sue over federal lending rule changes
cards.teaser: Housing advocacy organizations filed a lawsuit challenging new federal rules they say weaken fair lending protections.
cards.body:
Fair housing groups brought legal action against federal regulators over a rule change they argue removes protections against lending discrimination. The lawsuit targets the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau over modifications to small business lending data requirements.

The new rule narrows the scope of data collection requirements for small business lending. Housing advocates contend the changes weaken anti-discrimination regulations that had been in place to ensure equal access to credit.

cards.headline: Space stocks surge as SpaceX prepares for public offering
cards.teaser: Shares of space industry companies experienced sharp price increases ahead of SpaceX's anticipated IPO.
cards.body:
Stock prices for space industry companies including Rocket Lab and AST experienced significant gains, with some short sellers facing losses. The movements come as SpaceX prepares for what could be a record-breaking initial public offering.

Analysts have compared the trading activity to patterns seen in electric vehicle stocks during that sector's boom period. Market observers are watching multiple factors ahead of the SpaceX IPO, though some analysts have expressed reservations about valuations in the space sector.

hero.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after $1.2 million profit on Polymarket
hero.body:
Federal prosecutors charged a Google engineer with insider trading after he made $1.2 million through bets placed on Polymarket, a prediction market platform.

According to the complaint, the engineer wagered over $2.7 million on outcomes related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign. The charges suggest the employee used non-public information about the company's planned announcements to place informed bets on the platform.

Polymarket allows users to bet on real-world events, including corporate announcements, political outcomes, and cultural trends. The platform has grown in popularity as a venue for prediction markets, where participants can profit from correctly forecasting future events.

The case represents one of the first major insider trading prosecutions involving prediction markets rather than traditional stock trading. Prosecutors allege the Google employee exploited his position at the company to gain access to confidential information about which search terms and topics would be featured in the annual Year in Search report.

The Year in Search campaign is released by Google each year, highlighting the most popular search queries and trending topics over the previous 12 months. The report typically generates significant media attention and public interest.

By placing large wagers on Polymarket before the information became public, the engineer allegedly profited from advance knowledge of the campaign's contents. The complaint indicates he risked more than $2.7 million across multiple bets to generate the $1.2 million in profits.

Insider trading laws prohibit individuals from trading securities or other instruments based on material non-public information. While prediction markets operate differently from stock markets, prosecutors appear to be applying similar legal standards to wagers that rely on confidential corporate information.

The charges highlight growing regulatory scrutiny of prediction markets and how insider information might be exploited on these platforms. As prediction markets expand beyond traditional betting on elections and sports, prosecutors are examining whether existing securities laws apply to these new forms of wagering on corporate and economic events.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over contamination from firefighting foam
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed its largest lawsuit ever against the US manufacturer over chemicals at defense sites.
cards.body:
The Australian government has launched legal action against 3M, seeking damages exceeding A$2 billion over contamination from PFAS chemicals in firefighting foam. The case represents the largest legal claim ever brought by the Australian government.

Attorney General Michelle Rowland announced the lawsuit, which focuses on contamination at defense bases where the foam was used. PFAS, known as "forever chemicals," are per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances that persist in the environment and human body, raising significant health and environmental concerns.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's bid to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: The state civil rights agency defeated Tesla's attempt to throw out the case, with trial expected in July.
cards.body:
A California court rejected Tesla's attempt to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit brought by the state's civil rights agency. The agency hailed the decision as a win over the electric vehicle manufacturer.

The case is now expected to proceed to trial in July. California's civil rights agency filed the lawsuit alleging discriminatory practices at Tesla facilities within the state.

cards.headline: Rivian to deliver first R2 SUVs on June 9
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker set a date for customer deliveries of its new model.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the date for first customer deliveries of its new R2 SUV. The company is expanding its vehicle lineup with this new model.

CEO RJ Scaringe has called the R2 "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date," underscoring the significance of this release for the electric vehicle maker.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: The Psyche probe sent back high-resolution views of the red planet on its way to an asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft captured detailed images of Mars during a flyby of the planet. The probe photographed views of Mars' south pole and other surface features as it passed the red planet.

The spacecraft is traveling to a distant asteroid and used Mars for a gravity assist maneuver. The flyby provided an opportunity to collect unique imagery of the planet from the probe's trajectory and instruments.

cards.headline: Triomics raises $22 million for cancer center AI tools
cards.teaser: The oncology AI company secured Series B funding led by Battery Ventures.
cards.body:
Triomics has secured $22 million in Series B funding to develop artificial intelligence tools for oncology settings. Battery Ventures led the investment round.

The company is building AI applications tailored specifically for cancer centers, with the funding supporting the development and deployment of these specialized tools at cancer treatment facilities.

cards.headline: Nintendo adding Donkey Kong 64 to Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: The N64 game will join the subscription service's classic library on June 3.
cards.body:
Nintendo will add Donkey Kong 64 to its Switch Online subscription service next week. The Nintendo 64 game will become available to subscribers on June 3.

Donkey Kong 64 originally released in the 1990s for the N64 console. The game joins Nintendo's expanding library of classic titles available through the Switch Online Expansion Pack tier.

cards.headline: Google's AI struggles with basic spelling and word recognition
cards.teaser: The company's AI search feature has faced difficulties with simple words like disregard, stop, and ignore.
cards.body:
Google's AI tools have encountered significant problems with fundamental language tasks, including an inability to correctly spell the word "Google" itself. The search feature has also struggled to process and define common words such as "disregard," "stop," and "ignore."

The issues have drawn widespread attention and criticism, with multiple reports documenting the degraded performance across Google's AI search capabilities. The problems raise questions about the reliability of Google's AI systems during a competitive period in the AI industry.

hero.headline: Packers running back Josh Jacobs arrested on domestic violence charges
hero.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was arrested and faces multiple domestic violence charges, including felony strangulation. He was released from custody on Wednesday as the district attorney continues to review the case.

Jacobs faces five charges in total related to the domestic violence incident. The felony strangulation charge represents the most serious allegation among them. The Packers running back was taken into police custody earlier this week.

Authorities released Jacobs from jail on Wednesday while the investigation proceeds. The district attorney has not yet filed formal charges and is still evaluating the evidence in the case.

Jacobs joined the Packers before the 2025 season after spending his first five NFL seasons with the Las Vegas Raiders. He rushed for over 1,500 yards in 2022 and earned Pro Bowl honors that year.

The Packers have not publicly commented on Jacobs' arrest or his status with the team. The NFL has also not announced whether it will conduct its own investigation under the league's personal conduct policy.

Domestic violence cases in professional sports typically trigger both criminal proceedings and league discipline. The NFL's personal conduct policy allows the commissioner to place players on paid leave during investigations and to suspend players even if criminal charges are not filed.

The timing of the arrest comes during the offseason, with organized team activities underway across the league. Teams are preparing for training camps that will begin in July ahead of the 2026 season.

Jacobs' legal situation remains unresolved as prosecutors determine whether to move forward with charges. The district attorney's office has not provided a timeline for when a charging decision will be made.

cards.headline: Bipartisan Senate bill proposes reforms for college sports including salary cap and transfer limits
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell introduced legislation to address compensation, transfers and enforcement in college athletics.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell released a bipartisan bill targeting college sports reform. The legislation proposes creating a salary cap system and limiting player transfers between schools.

The bill also includes provisions aimed at preventing coach poaching after recent high-profile moves, including Lane Kiffin's jump to LSU. The legislation addresses eligibility rules and enforcement mechanisms across college athletics programs.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey subpoena FIFA over World Cup ticket pricing
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from both states opened an investigation into complaints about high ticket prices for the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
New York and New Jersey's attorneys general have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The subpoena seeks information about FIFA's ticket sales and pricing strategies, with the probe announced by New York's Letitia James and New Jersey's Jennifer Davenport.

The investigation focuses on matches at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Complaints center on fans being misled about seat locations and FIFA's public messaging contributing to inflated ticket prices throughout the tournament.

cards.headline: Georgia coach Kirby Smart suggests SEC could leave NCAA
cards.teaser: The Georgia football coach said he would support the conference breaking away to operate under its own rules.
cards.body:
Georgia head football coach Kirby Smart raised the possibility of the SEC leaving the NCAA to operate independently. Smart said he would support the conference creating its own governance structure and playing by its own rules.

The comments come amid ongoing debates about conference expansion and how college athletics should be structured. Multiple sources reported that SEC leaders are discussing contingency plans, though no formal action has been taken toward separating from the NCAA.

cards.headline: Crystal Palace win Conference League with victory over Rayo Vallecano
cards.teaser: Jean-Philippe Mateta scored as Crystal Palace won the European club competition under manager Oliver Glasner.
cards.body:
Crystal Palace won their first European trophy by defeating Rayo Vallecano 1-0 in the Conference League final in Leipzig. Jean-Philippe Mateta scored the decisive goal in what proved to be manager Oliver Glasner's final match in charge.

The victory was particularly significant for Palace, who finished 15th in the Premier League. As Conference League winners, they have secured a place in next season's Europa League—a spot they would not have earned through their league position. The triumph comes a year after Palace were denied Europa League qualification despite winning the FA Cup due to UEFA's multi-club ownership regulations.

cards.headline: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson calls coaching changes a breath of fresh air
cards.teaser: The two-time MVP discussed offseason changes within the Baltimore organization and his commitment to the team.
cards.body:
Lamar Jackson described the coaching changes made by the Baltimore Ravens during the offseason as refreshing. The quarterback addressed the shifts in the organization's staff during organized team activities.

Jackson declined to discuss his contract negotiations but said his commitment to the Ravens has not changed. He indicated he wants to move past previous discussions about a fully guaranteed contract deal.

cards.headline: SEC leaders criticize College Football Playoff metrics explanation
cards.teaser: Conference officials objected to how the playoff selection committee explained its strength of schedule calculations.
cards.body:
Leaders from the Southeastern Conference criticized the College Football Playoff's explanation of how it weighs strength of schedule in team selection. The dispute centers on which metrics the committee uses to evaluate teams.

The debate has intensified as conferences discuss playoff expansion and selection criteria. SEC officials argue the current system does not adequately account for the difficulty of their conference schedule compared to teams in other leagues.

cards.headline: Tennis player Jakub Mensik collapses on court after French Open win
cards.teaser: The player said his body shut down following a second-round match played in high heat at the Paris tournament.
cards.body:
Jakub Mensik collapsed on court after winning his second-round match at the French Open in a gruelling five-set contest against Mariano Navone that lasted over four and a half hours. The tennis player said his body "just turned off" due to the extreme heat in Paris, and he required a wheelchair to return to the locker room.

Mensik criticised the conditions as "insane," highlighting the limited time available to cool down between changeovers. His collapse prompted calls from other players, including Novak Djokovic, for organisers to schedule more matches later in the day during periods of extreme heat.
